notes: A second real 2560x1440 capture, all twelve heroes named by the player.
This is the fixture that pins the grid search. Before it existed the
search chose pitch 101 where the truth is 117, which still put ten of
twelve boxes over a real portrait -- just the wrong one each time, so
the whole roster came out shifted by a slot and every score still looked
healthy. Ranking candidate pitches by a cheap pass over nominal boxes put
the correct one eleventh of nineteen; only refining the slots before
It also cross-validates the learned variants. Apollo and Silver have
reference art that does not match what the game draws, and their
variants were taken from the other 2560x1440 fixture -- a different
match, different framing. They are expected to read correctly here off
art learned there, which is the whole point of the variant mechanism.
The background behind this strip is a flat tan wall, close in colour to
the amber backplate, which is what broke the self-slot probe until it
started comparing chroma rather than RGB.
